facts.statement: The genus Rapaxavis was described by Morschhauser and colleagues in 2009.
The type species of the genus is Rapaxavis pani.
Rapaxavis is classified as a genus of enantiornithean bird.
facts.quote: Rapaxavis a genus of enantiornithean bird.

facts.statement: A specimen discovered by Pan Lijun in 2006 was initially referred to the genus Longirostravis before being reclassified.
facts.quote: In 2006 a specimen was reported, discovered by Pan Lijun at Xiaioyugou near the town of Lianhe, and referred to Longirostravis.

facts.statement: The specimen was formally named Rapaxavis pani in 2009 by a team including Eric M. Morschhauser and David Varricchio.
facts.quote: In 2009 this specimen was named and described as the type species Rapaxavis pani by Eric M. Morschhauser, David Varricchio, Gao Chunling, Liu Jinyuan, Wang Xuri, Cheng Xiadong and Meng Qingjin.

facts.statement: The genus name Rapaxavis means "grasping bird" and refers to the special grasping function of the animal's foot.
facts.quote: The generic name combines the Latin rapax, "grasping", with avis, "bird", in reference to the special grasping function of the foot.

facts.statement: The species name pani honors Pan Lijun, the discoverer of the fossil.
facts.quote: The specific name honours Pan as discoverer.

facts.statement: The species name also alludes to Pan, the Greek god of forests, reflecting the assumption that the bird lived in trees.
facts.quote: It is also an allusion to Pan, the god of the forests, because the species was assumed to have been arboreal.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen DMNH D2522 was found in the Jiufotang Formation dating to the early Albian stage.
facts.quote: The holotype, DMNH D2522, was found in a layer of the Jiufotang Formation dating from the early Albian.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a nearly complete skeleton including the skull preserved on a slab.
facts.quote: It consists of a nearly complete skeleton with skull, on a slab.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen represents a subadult individual.
Initial preparation of the skeleton damaged it, specifically removing the entire right jugal bone from the skull.
facts.quote: Later it was prepared but in an unprofessional way, damaging the skeleton, especially the skull where the entire right jugal bone was removed.

facts.statement: Further preparation at the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County repaired some of the damage caused to the skeleton.
facts.quote: Subsequently, it was sent to the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County where a further preparation took place, which managed to repair some of the damage.

facts.statement: A more detailed redescription of the species was published in 2011 based on knowledge gained during the repair process.
facts.quote: The knowledge gained during this process was the basis for a more detailed redescription in 2011.

facts.statement: Rapaxavi belongs to the extinct subclass Enantiornithes.
The animal is classified within the extinct family Longipterygidae.
Fossils of Rapaxavis were recovered from the Early Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation in Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: Sus restos fósiles fueron recuperados en estratos del Cretácico Inferior de la Formación Jiufotang en Liaoning, en la República Popular de China.

facts.statement: Rapaxavis lived during the Aptian stage, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)
